There is a (not really -- see 2nd msg) mistake in FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.castLE. With the current definition, if m is 1, n is 6, h : m ≤ n, φ : L.BoundedFormula α mis (&0 = &1).allwith only one bounded variable &0, then φ.castLE h becomes (&0 = &1).all with TWO bounded variables &0 and &1. The correct definition should be (&0 = &6).all

The inductive case all should involve a liftAt. However, if we define with liftAt (n - m) m, the target type becomes L.BoundedFormula α (m + (n - m)) which is different from L.BoundedFormula α n.

My suggestion to avoid these casting issues is to define castAdd instead of castLE. This form will match with liftUp as both the target models will be L.BoundedFormula α (n + n'). There will still be casting involved in some lemmas, such as between L.BoundedFormula α (n + n' + n'')and L.BoundedFormula α (n + (n' + n'')) in castAdd_castAdd, but that will be a lot easier to handle than the subtraction n - m.
Maybe castLE is not intended to keep the semantic meaning. Then everything works fine with liftAt if we want to keep the semantic meaning. But the name castLE is indeed misleading.
